allocation_status: Teaching design; verified table gives no official lesson allocation.
rationale: Twelve 40-minute lessons separate microorganism groups, economic roles, transmission, infection types and route-matched prevention, followed by food preservation, a teacher-controlled mould-growth inquiry option, evidence limits and a community message draft. The curriculum gives six outcomes, three content bullets and a multi-step project; the chosen count is a design allocation, not an official source count. Multi-day observation, if approved, spans lessons and teacher-supervised intervals.
prerequisites: Basic distinctions among fungi, bacteria and viruses; sources must be teacher-reviewed.
Evidence-based classification and simple cause-versus-association reasoning.
Safe food handling, privacy, and respect when discussing infection and prevention.
teacher_confirmation_required: Preview current, age-appropriate public-health sources and select non-stigmatising infection examples and route-specific prevention claims.

Approve any sealed food-substrate observation, allergies/materials, teacher preparation, sample location, observation window and safe disposal; pupils never open, touch, smell, incubate at body temperature or take samples home.
If no approved actual investigation occurs, use clearly labelled supplied images/data and do not report student performance or observed growth.
Approve the food-preservation sources and verify that no activity leads learners to taste, consume, prepare or take home classroom samples.
Preview any digital source and provide an equivalent print option; record actual digital use separately from a written research response.
Approve any community message before delivery; a draft/poster is not evidence that community sensitisation happened.
Confirm 40-minute pacing, accessibility, privacy protections and further opportunities for actions not observed.

lesson_map.title: How can microorganisms reach a person?
Which infections are fungal, bacterial or viral?
Does each prevention measure match the route?
How are prevention and control connected?
Which food-preservation choice fits the evidence?
How could a mould-growth investigation be made safe?
How can a preservation message stay accurate?
How do route, prevention and daily life connect?

assessment_tasks.evidence_scope: Actual sealed observation requires teacher approval and named observation; supplied images/data are not performed evidence.
A draft is not evidence of an approved or delivered community sensitisation activity.

performance_evidence.inquiry: Actual observation of sealed substrate changes requires approved setup and a named learner observation; supplied records do not certify this action.
performance_evidence.digital: Actual use of an approved digital source must be observed separately; print work is an equivalent option, not digital-use evidence.
performance_evidence.community: A written food-preservation message is a draft; delivery to a community requires approval and separate observation.
performance_evidence.attitude: A respectful evidence-based response can be observed in the task; it does not establish a lasting disposition.
